standard.title: Multiply larger numbers
standard.description: Solve problems involving multiplication of larger numbers by one- or two-digit numbers, choosing efficient calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; check the reasonableness of answers
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can multiply and divide by powers of 10 and apply multiplication to practical problems (AC9M4N05). They have not yet used efficient written strategies for multiplying larger numbers by two-digit numbers.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve problems involving multiplication of larger numbers by one- or two-digit numbers, choosing efficient strategies and checking reasonableness.

nodes.label: Mental and informal multiplication strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply and explain mental strategies for multiplication including doubling, halving and place value partitioning.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two mental strategies to multiply a two- or three-digit number by a single digit; explain the strategy used.
nodes.typical_width: Select and justify mental strategies (doubling/halving, near doubles, place value partitioning); apply to a range of two-digit by one-digit calculations.
wider: Compare strategy efficiency across different number types
Use mental strategies to estimate before calculating

response_modes.reason: Students who have only one multiplication strategy cannot adapt to different number types. Building a repertoire of mental strategies gives flexibility and supports estimation.

success_criteria: Student applies at least two distinct mental strategies correctly
Student can explain why a chosen strategy is efficient for a given calculation

nodes.label: Standard written algorithm for larger numbers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply a written algorithm to multiply a multi-digit number by a one-digit number, showing working.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly apply a written multiplication algorithm (e.g. long multiplication) to a 3-digit × 1-digit problem.
nodes.typical_width: Apply the standard algorithm to 3- and 4-digit numbers by 1-digit; connect algorithm steps to place value; identify where trades occur.
wider: Compare multiple written algorithm forms (area model, lattice method, standard algorithm)
Investigate how the algorithm works for numbers with zeros in the middle

response_modes.reason: Procedural accuracy with the standard algorithm requires practice; errors in carrying/trading cluster here and propagate to two-digit multiplications if not addressed.

nodes.hinge_reason: Trading/carrying errors in 1-digit multiplication propagate directly into Node 3 — students who cannot reliably carry in 3-digit × 1-digit problems produce systematic errors in two-digit multiplication.
success_criteria: Student completes a 3-digit × 1-digit multiplication using a written algorithm correctly
Student identifies and explains where any trading steps occur

nodes.label: Two-digit multiplication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can multiply a larger number by a two-digit number using a chosen strategy, explaining the process.
nodes.minimum_width: Multiply a 2- or 3-digit number by a two-digit number using at least one written or mental strategy; show the calculation steps.
nodes.typical_width: Apply the area model and/or standard algorithm to 3-digit × 2-digit; compare methods; use digital tools to check.
wider: Investigate real-world scaling contexts (e.g. catering, construction estimates)
Explore multiplication of numbers just below a round number using compensation strategies

response_modes.reason: Two-digit multiplication has diverse efficient strategies. Students who only know one approach are at risk when it's inefficient. Real contexts motivate method choice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Area model, algorithm, mental compensation — genuine method comparison is rich for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student multiplies a larger number by a two-digit number and obtains the correct answer
Student shows the full calculation process

nodes.label: Checking reasonableness
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can estimate the result of a multiplication and use estimation to check the reasonableness of a calculated answer.
nodes.minimum_width: Estimate a multiplication result by rounding to a convenient number and compare to the calculated answer; judge whether the answer is reasonable.
nodes.typical_width: Apply estimation before and after calculation; identify unreasonable results; explain what estimation strategy was used.
wider: Apply in financial contexts: checking estimated costs against calculated totals
Investigate how the choice of rounding affects estimate accuracy
success_criteria: Student produces a reasonable estimate before or after calculating
Student correctly judges whether a given answer is reasonable using estimation
